blocks.value: An exception is an event that disrupts a program's normal flow while it's running. Exception handling is how you intercept that disruption and respond to it instead of letting the program crash.
Checked exceptions are caught by the compiler before the program even runs:

Exception                Description
ClassNotFoundException   The class is not found.
IllegalAccessException   Access to a class is denied.
InstantiationException   Attempt to create an object of an abstract class or interface.
NoSuchMethodException    A requested method does not exist.
Unchecked exceptions (also called runtime exceptions) only surface while the program is actually executing:

Exception                          Description
ArithmeticException                Arithmetic error, such as dividing an integer by 0
ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException     Accessing an invalid index of an array
ArrayStoreException                Assigning a value to an array index of the wrong type
InputMismatchException             Entering a value that doesn't match the expected type
NullPointerException               Invalid use of a null reference
NumberFormatException              Invalid conversion of a string to a numeric format
StringIndexOutOfBoundsException    Accessing an invalid index of a string
